subject: Safety-net fee structure and commit phasing for elastic headroom
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@orbitalai.com>

Subject: Question on 'safety-net' fee for short burst headroom

Hi Priyom,

We ran into a short window last week where our ingestion spiked and we exceeded our committed throughput for about 2 hours. Your support team mentioned a 'safety-net' fee in addition to the overrun rate — can you explain how that is computed and whether it scales down for one-off usage? We are evaluating whether to (a) raise committed baseline, (b) pay the ad-hoc overrun, or (c) sign a short-term protected headroom add-on.

Two asks:
- A simple worked example with $/token and a per-window safety-net surcharge (if any).
- Any discount/packaging you can offer if we commit to a phased ramp (Q4 ramp to full commit H1).

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

Elena
Elena Morales
Head of Platform
Orbital AI

Subject: Re: Question on 'safety-net' fee for short burst headroom

Hi Elena — thanks for the note and the spike log. Appreciate the context. Short answer: the safety-net is intended to smooth economics for customers who occasionally exceed committed throughput because of unpredictable events, but it’s priced to discourage chronic overrun (so there are two levers: higher overrun unit rate and a small fixed surcharge for protection windows).

I attached a one-page term sheet and a toy calculation. High-level:
- Overrun unit rate: committed tier rate * 1.8 (per-token basis) after free threshold within the window.
- Safety-net surcharge: flat $/hour for a reserved headroom window (configurable 1–72 hrs); it caps the per-hour exposure and makes billing predictable.
- Phased-commit discount: if you agree to a 3-stage ramp (Nov -> Jan -> Apr) with minimum CU (committed units) jumps, we can offer a stepped discount that reduces the overrun multiplier to 1.45 at full commit.

See attached term sheet: 20260901-safety-net-term-sheet.pdf and a follow-up worksheet I'll send with Ben that maps this to your last 6 weeks of usage. If that looks okay, we can draft a short addendum and a DocuSign.

Quick Q: would you want the safety-net priced per-region (US/EU) or a single global headroom?

Thanks — Priyom
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: 20260901-safety-net-term-sheet.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 11:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on 'safety-net' fee for short burst headroom

Elena — adding a concrete example inline to make this actionable. Using your spike CSV (sample summarized): peak 6M tokens over 2 hours, baseline commit equivalent 1.5M tokens/hour.

Option A — Ad-hoc overrun (no safety-net):
- Committed unit rate: $0.0025/token
- Overrun multiplier: 1.8x (ad-hoc) => $0.0045/token for excess tokens
- Billing impact (6M peak, 3M excess): 3M * $0.0045 = $13,500

Option B — 8-hour safety-net window (reserved headroom):
- Safety-net surcharge: $850 / 8-hr window (flat)
- Overrun multiplier while inside safety-net: 1.25x => $0.003125/token
- Billing impact: excess 3M * $0.003125 = $9,375 + $850 = $10,225 (savings vs A = $3,275)

Option C — Phased commit (3-stage):
- Immediate small uplift to CU for Q4, full commit by Apr. We offer a phased discount: 5% (stage1), 7.5% (stage2), 12% (full). Overrun multiplier at full commit reduces to 1.45x ($0.003625/token). If you hit expected ramp metrics we also waive the safety-net surcharge for two ad-hoc windows per year.

Recommendation: if spikes are rare and predictable, safety-net window is cheapest for single incidents; if you expect sustained growth, phased commit lowers long-term unit economics.

Next steps: I put together a commit phasing worksheet and a sample addendum (see attachment 20260902-commit-phasing-proposal.xlsx). Priyom — can you confirm legal should see a short addendum (yes/no)? Elena — I can join a 30-min call Thurs to walk these numbers.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
